I have a mouse. Not one of those pesky ones that gnaw through kitchen cupboards at night and leave unpleasant gifts in the corners of the house. No, I don't need a cat with a hunter's soul to rid me of bothersome guests.

My mouse enters the house through the door like the rest of the inhabitants, and it even has a passport. It's a silver-grey Russian hamster with a dark stripe down its back. It eats hamster food (although it doesn't like it) and takes long sand baths in a tiny dish it has in its house. And what a house it has...

Two floors just for him, with play areas, a bedroom, pantry, bathroom, and even a small gym!

My mouse eats a lot and is slightly overweight, specifically, it’s fifty milligrams too heavy. But we forgive him because he exercises a lot and reluctantly eats the diet food we give him. Occasionally, we give him a piece of bread or a nut.

He grabs the food with his little hands, sits down, brings it to his mouth, and moves his whiskers with determination. If we reach for the food as if to take it away, he abruptly turns and moves away. If we insist too much, he pushes us away with his hand but never bites. It's clear he's a male and territorial.

My mouse exercises at night. At around nine every evening, without fail, he comes out of his bedroom, takes a quick sand bath, and climbs onto his wheel to run. Interestingly, he always runs in the same direction. Sometimes I wonder what he expects to find at the end of the path or what strange reason drives him to go that way. He’s very clever and also uses the wheel to entertain us... If he sees us having dinner, he runs on it for a while and then approaches the bars with a clear attitude of "I want my reward." He shows off his skills to earn treats from us.

Sometimes we put him inside a transparent plastic ball so he can run around the house and explore secret corners. He doesn't like open spaces at all and always seeks out corners. He gets scared when the floor is slippery, like the bathroom or kitchen floors. He likes walking on bedding.

My mouse pees behind the door. He's very clean, really. He takes sand baths and spends a lot of time licking his hands to groom himself and stay nice and clean. One of his little houses is a toy mushroom, specifically, Smurfette's house from the cartoon. The house has a plastic door that swings on tiny hinges. We leave the door open so he can make a nest or pantry inside. He uses the gap between the open door and the mushroom to accumulate kitchen paper and use it as a bathroom.

He likes the entire cage to have his scent. He’s male and wants to dominate his territory. That's why, when we clean the cage and put new bedding on the floor, he spends several busy hours, dragging himself around and rubbing the bedding on his belly with determination. He doesn’t want anyone to mistake it for another’s territory and settle in his home.

My mouse gives kisses. Sometimes, we hold him in the palm of our hand and pet his back with the other. He’s naturally nervous, driven by instincts to feel constantly in danger, instincts which I understand have helped his species survive in the wild.

Despite this, when we pet him like this, he becomes calm and relaxed. After a while, if he's in a good mood, he sticks out his incredibly long tongue and starts licking the fingers of the hand holding him. He appreciates the mouse massages we give him.

My mouse has a wet nose. He has an excellent sense of smell, much better than his eyesight. In fact, he doesn't see well up close. But nothing escapes his sense of smell. When he's healthy, his nose is wet.

My mouse has a doctor. He’s had a couple of health issues... a urinary infection and some arthritis in his front paws. We put in softer bedding so he doesn't have to exert himself as much to walk, and he improved very quickly.

We treated the urinary infection with a few (very few) milligrams of medication. We had to give him the medicine twice a day, and he didn't like it much. He tried to push us away with his little hands and ran off when we were done. But I'm sure he appreciated it because it must have hurt to pee.

My mouse goes on vacation. When we’re away, we take him to my parents' house, and he enjoys a good vacation because my parents, like good grandparents, indulge him with treats.

My mouse is happy because he lives in a happy home. We love him very much and will miss him dearly when he’s no longer with us. Nonetheless, I’m sure we’ll remember him fondly through these words, his photos, and his papers. Mouse papers.
